newsitem.title: USA: Mass. supreme court hears congressional fight.
newsitem.headline: Mass. supreme court hears congressional fight.

text.p: The battle to become the Democratic nominee for a Massachusetts congressional seat moved to the state's highest court Monday.

Philip Johnston, who learned Friday while campaigning with first lady Hillary Clinton that a state court ruled his opponent, William Delahunt, won the Sept 17 Democratic primary, filed suit today with the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts.

Johnston 52, a liberal and former state representative who lacked funds for a television campaign in the primary, was initially declared the winner by a 206 vote margin. After a recount in selected districts certified by Secretary of State William Galvin, his lead had shrunk to 175.

But Norfolk Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Donovan ruled, after a review of more than 900 challenged ballots, that Delahunt, the Norfolk district attorney, actually won the race by 108 votes. She ordered Galvin to print new ballots with Delahunt's name.

Now Johnston is asking the state's highest judges to review those same ballots and order that two sets of ballots be printed for the Nov. 5 election - one with his name on them and one with Delahunt's.
"We believe these are not votes. We believe they were counted blank on the ballots and they should be counted blank by the courts," Johnston's lawyer Dennis Newman told reporters.

The ballots in question are punch-card types where the voter punches out the name of the person he or she is supporting. The problem arose because some of the ballots were not punched through completely.
A court hearing is scheduled for later on Monday.
